RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

The panel's composition alone proves nothing — in economics departments, an all-male panel can simply reflect who is senior there. It is not evidence of bias, and leading with it will make you look like you're arguing from demographics rather than facts.

It does matter as context, and in many public-sector systems gender balance on selection panels is a formal requirement; check your university's rules and your national equality act.

Your real case is the qualification gap: completed PhD vs. unfinished, six papers vs. two, four years teaching. That's where the burden shifts to them to justify weighting "industry experience."

Send a written follow-up citing your legal right to a reasoned decision, with a deadline. Mention composition factually, once.
